subject: english
title: Compound Sentence Crew · Q2 W04 D03
objective: Identify two complete ideas joined in a compound sentence.
introduction: Two complete ideas can join hands with and, but, or so! 🐱✨ Help Milo spot them.

vocabulary.definition: A sentence that joins two complete ideas.
A word such as and, but, or so that connects ideas.
A group of words that tells who or what and what happened.

items.prompt: Which group of words gives a complete thought?
items.explanation: “I read” and “Milo listens” are both complete ideas joined by and.

items.prompt: Which choice has a subject and an action?

options.text: It rained, so we stayed inside.

items.explanation: “It rained” and “we stayed inside” are two complete ideas joined by so.

items.prompt: Which sentence tells a whole idea?

options.text: I wanted to play, but I had homework.

items.explanation: But joins “I wanted to play” and “I had homework” — two complete ideas in one sentence.

items.prompt: Which example can stand alone as a sentence?
items.explanation: Both parts of “Ana sings, and Ben claps” can stand alone, so and joins them.

items.prompt: Which group is complete and clear?
items.explanation: Both sides are complete ideas joined by and, so the sentence is clear and complete.
